data.title: macOS 27: new Siri takes on AI productivity apps
data.description:
The two most noticeable things about macOS 27 Golden Gate are the newly updated Siri AI and the design changes that make windows and icons more consistent. Siri AI offers the same features and capabilities as on iOS 27, but the Mac gives it access to different context — and new ways to be useful.

Over the last few years, apps and browsers have tried to learn more about your work and what you want to use AI assistants for, so they can better answer your questions or perform tasks. Today, many top web browsers, excluding Safari, come with a sidebar-based AI assistant that can look at one or multiple open tabs to provide contextual answers. Apps like Highlight, Caddy, and Littlebird can also look at your current window, then use that information as context for your queries.

The new Siri is similar. You can invoke Siri anywhere on your screen, allowing it to answer questions about what it sees, summarize information, or provide you with more details. For instance, if you are looking at an item you want to purchase, you could ask Siri to show you alternative options too.

Instead of having Siri look at the whole page, you can also select a part of the page via Apple’s new Visual Intelligence features. If you press Command + Shift + Space, you can add the currently focused window to your context for the AI.

To select a specific part, you press Command + Shift +6 to bring up a crosshair selection tool. After this, you can directly ask a question or perform an image search. Based on your selection, you will also get shortcuts like “select,” “add to contact,” and “look up location.”

Apple has also improved Spotlight Search on Mac. You can directly ask Siri questions within Spotlight to get answers from the web, and you now you can also select Applications, Files, Actions, and Clipboard to search within that particular area of context. Plus, Spotlight now allows you to run Shortcuts or look up your recent search history.

Since Siri has access to your files, emails, and messages, you’re able to search for a variety of things that you couldn’t before. In tests, I pulled up membership IDs without opening my files, asked for details about an upcoming trip, and looked up the embargo date for an upcoming news story in the works. While I don’t find Spotlight as advanced as the highly extensible Mac productivity tool Raycast, it’s still much better than before.

Siri can also now help you with reviewing documents or performing writing tasks. Since the desktop is one of the better surfaces for writing long text, I found it to be more useful here than on the iPhone. You can do things like select a block of text and ask Siri to proofread it, improve it, or rewrite it. You can also ask Siri to draft something for you within any text box.

Safari, meanwhile, has added AI-powered page tracking, which is useful for keeping an eye on things like price drops, privacy policy changes, or new blog posts on pages when there is no RSS support. Plus, Safari can automatically organize tabs based on topics, which is handy.

One small but neat new feature is that when you download a file or rename it, the system suggests a name based on context in the Finder or when you’re saving the document.

Apart from Siri, macOS 27 Golden Gate brings design changes with new Liquid Glass icons, an adjustable slider for Liquid Glass design, and a better way to “diffuse” content when you move windows around.

The company said that app windows have a more consistent corner radius. Sidebars now stretch edge-to-edge and have new colorful icons. The new operating system update also better highlights active windows.

The OS update additionally adds features like enhanced child safety controls, shared cross-platform photo albums, and an updated eraser, better search in email, app resizing for iPhone mirroring, and quick suggestions for adding events to the calendar.

macOS 27 Golden Gate is available starting today for MacBook Air and MacBook Pro 2020 version with Apple Silicon or later, iMac with Apple Silicon (2021 or later), Mac Mini (2020 or later), Mac Studio (2022 or later), Mac Pro (2023 or later), and MacBook Neo. You can go to System Settings > General > Software Update to get the latest version.

data.title: With iOS 27, I’m actually using Siri again
data.description:
For years, I barely used Siri for anything beyond menial tasks like setting timers or alarms. That has changed with iOS 27, as I now go back to Siri for complex requests and to make sense of on-screen context again and again.

While Siri is clearly front and center in this software update by Apple, I also enjoy many of the other quality-of-life updates.

Siri

I have been using iOS 27 on my main device since the public beta version was released, and on another device through the developer beta before that. I have really enjoyed using the new Siri, often trying to find new use cases for it — and that’s possibly the biggest win for Apple, given that I, like many people, had given up on Siri befor this update.

Over two years ago, Apple introduced Apple Intelligence and teased an advanced version of Siri. And after multiple delays, the company is finally shipping it, and it doesn’t disappoint. Built on the back of Google’s Gemini models, Siri is much smarter than its previous version that was built on extended knowledge and a shaky ChatGPT integration. It also has a new logo and transition animation.

For starters, I asked Siri about several different things in the area of sports, ranging from World Cup matches to team lineups and scores. There were some hiccups in the earlier developer versions, but most of the information was correct. Siri can also take complex, multi-step directions. For instance, I asked it to find small or hidden and useful features for iOS 27 and add them to a note, and it did a good job of that.

Plus, Siri can draft a message for you and send it to someone.

And because Siri can fetch context from your files, messages, and email, you can also ask it to look up a conversation, like one related to a delivery, and have it create a message for returns.

Siri’s on-screen context was a big blessing, too. I could ask trivial questions like the oldest player on the pitch when I was looking at line-ups for two teams in the World Cup, or have it read the text on screen out loud when I didn’t want to read. When I was looking at a startup’s website, I could ask Siri to look up its funding information and competitors.

One of my favorite use cases was surfing around coffee Reddit for new roasters and beans, and asking Siri to add it to a specific note. I did face a few difficulties in getting Siri to add it to the right note, but eventually I dumbed down the note’s name for better consistency.

The Camera app also now has Siri access, which means you can ask questions about things that are visible in your viewfinder. When I was at a restaurant, I asked Siri what drink I was holding. Because of the color of the drink, it said This is green juice, which is a good first visual assumption. When I specified that I was at an Indian restaurant, it correctly said this could be Jaljeera or Aam Panna. (It was the latter).

I also took a photo of the restaurant’s sign and asked Siri to suggest the best items from its menu. Another use case that works better now is that, when you take a photo of a coffee bag, you can ask Siri for the best way to brew the coffee.

With iOS 27, Siri AI gets a dedicated app that lets you return to your previous chats. In Settings, users can change Siri’s voice and expressiveness, as well.

The new assistant is positioned to work with other, third-party apps, and as developers update their apps after the operating system rolls out, it will be interesting to see if there is a smooth handoff between Siri and apps.

Apple Intelligence

Apple Intelligence powers a number of AI features in iOS 27.

For instance, Apple has sprinkled vibe-coding features within iOS 27. The first is a Shortcuts creation feature that lets you describe shortcuts and automations in natural language to create them. That means you can start with a simple request, like “Show me today’s to-do items every morning at 8 am” or “convert photo to JPEG,” instead of having to figure out how to craft the shortcut yourself. After the shortcut is created, you can make it more complex by adding more steps, like “convert selected photos to JPEG and share them through AirDrop.”

I personally always wanted to create a list of songs that I listened to and liked in bars and cafes, so I made a shortcut to Shazam the song and save both the track and location.

You can also now create a custom alert in Safari to track changes to a page like a blog, item pricing, or a privacy policy page.

The Photos app has some new handy tools like “reframe” and “extend.” I found they don’t always work that well, but in some cases, they can make an image look better. Meanwhile, Apple has definitely improved its eraser functionality, which now leaves fewer strange artifacts when you remove an object.

With Apple Intelligence, when you get certain messages such as information for an event or location, smart suggestions will ask if you’d like to add them to your Calendar or Notes. What’s more, the Passwords app can now automatically change passwords on your behalf by logging into a site.

Other quality-of-life improvements

Before discussing any other features, I have to say that I love the new clipboard feature. This now lets you paste anything — including links, photos, videos, and text — from one app to another easily. Once the item is in your clipboard, you see a shortcut button saying “paste from Safari” (or similar) on the keyboard, which lets you paste the item. I have been using this feature so frequently, and I can’t stress enough how life-changing this is despite it being a small change.

iOS 27 also addresses people’s gripes about how the Liquid Glass design looked. With the operating system update, users can now change the transparency of the Liquid Glass design based on their preferences. The control is granular, so you don’t have to choose from presets, either.

Apple also introduced intelligent network switching in this update, which automatically flips the connection from Wi-Fi to mobile data if there are issues with the wireless connection. The switching is seamless and very handy when you are doing important work, so you don’t lose your internet connection.

The update focuses a lot on child safety as well, as it includes a new setup flow that automatically recommends essential apps. Plus, parents can set schedules, time limits, and allowances for different days of the week. Guardians can also get notifications when children are accessing new websites and can approve that access remotely. And the system displays a warning when children are exposed to nudity in Messages, FaceTime, and other apps.

Besides Siri AI, iOS 27 doesn’t have many marquee features, but it makes everyday life much easier. In previous years, I would have defaulted to going to ChatGPT or Gemini to get answers of a question. But with iOS 27, I find myself using Siri more often, even though I don’t live in Apple’s Messages and Mail apps.

iOS 27 is rolling out to all users with iPhone 11 or later and iPhone SE (2nd gen) or later. Users can go to Settings > General > Software Update to download the latest version.

data.title: Fashion app Daydream uses Apple Intelligence to help you shop the outfits in your camera roll
data.description:
Daydream, an AI-powered fashion discovery app, launched two new features on Monday to let iPhone users turn saved outfit photos into shoppable results and search for clothing and accessories through Siri, without opening the app.

The new features were built using Apple’s iOS 27 developer tools, which officially rolled out today. To use either feature, you’ll need an iPhone running iOS 27 with Siri AI enabled, along with the Daydream app installed. The app is free to download on iOS devices.

The first feature uses Apple’s image-context capabilities, letting users shop from images already saved in their Photos app. Daydream analyzes the outfit in the image, identifies its individual pieces, and automatically surfaces shoppable matches and similar styles from Daydream’s catalog of roughly 3 million products.

That means a screenshot of an outfit found on Instagram or Pinterest could become the starting point for a shopping search. Daydream can break down the image into relevant items, such as a sweater, pants, shoes, or accessories, and match them with products available through its collection. If the exact item in the photo is still available, Daydream can match the image back to the retailer selling it. If it’s no longer available, the app will instead surface similar options.

It can also handle requests for variations on what appears in an image. “I like this sweater but want it in red,” for example, is the kind of request Daydream can understand, Julie Bornstein, co-founder and CEO of Daydream, explained to TechCrunch.

The second feature is a Siri-powered natural-language search function. Users can make requests by voice or text through Siri without having to open Daydream’s app.

A user could say, “Hey Siri, search Daydream for a cool blazer for my board meeting on Monday,” and Daydream then provides results personalized to them.

Bornstein adds that the experience can be more tailored if users have set up Daydream’s “Style Passport,” which asks for details such as their sizes, preferred brands, personal style, and budget.

The company joins a growing number of AI shopping tools designed to rethink product discovery, such as big names like Google and Amazon, as well as some smaller players like Onton and Alta. But Bornstein believes that Daydream’s latest features offer something special that a lot of these other tools just can’t match.

“Most visual search tools don’t have the fashion category expertise, so they return results that don’t feel accurate, from brands that aren’t credible, or they link you to non-shoppable images,” she said. 

The launch fits into Daydream’s broader bet on AI-powered fashion shopping. The company sees these new features as more than standalone shopping tools. Its longer-term ambition is to build a shopping agent.

“This is one step toward the bigger vision, [which is] a shopping agent that understands someone’s style well enough to work across every surface in their life, not just on one surface,” Bornstein said. “Expect us to keep going deeper into on-device intelligence and further into the everyday moments where people are already discovering things they want.”

Daydream’s app launched last year and touts that it has more than 1.5 million shoppers browsing products from more than 325 retailers and 10,000 brands. Its retail lineup includes brands such as Anthropologie, Dolce & Gabbana, Uniqlo, J.Crew, Reformation, Gucci, and Nordstrom.

data.title: Microsoft’s new AI ‘code of conduct’ tells models not to hack systems or trick humans
data.description:
As the AI world shifts its focus to safety and alignment, Microsoft has released a new AI code of conduct meant to guide AI models away from dangerous behavior.

The document is more low-level than Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s recent call for pacing the frontier, instead focusing on the values and red lines that guide model training within Microsoft AI. Still, the result is a comprehensive guide as to how Microsoft approaches AI safety, and how those ideas are implemented in practice.

The document begins with the prediction that, in the next decade, superintelligent AI systems will surpass human performance in most tasks. “Containing, controlling, and aligning such a powerful force is one of the greatest challenges humanity has ever faced,” the code of conduct continues. “We must therefore be completely clear about why we are inventing these systems and how we intend to control them.”

The code of conduct also lays out general principles that Microsoft AI models should uphold — supporting humans rather than replacing them, for instance, and accelerating human flourishing — as well as specific safety constraints meant to implement those principles.

Under Microsoft’s system, each model has an overarching code of conduct that overrides the preferences of individual users or any specific tasks. That includes “absolute constraints” forbidding cyberattacks, nuclear weapons, or deepfake production. It also includes broader provisions against a general loss of human control.

“MAI Models will not use adaptive, deceptive, self-reinforcing, collusion, or other mechanisms to evade or defeat human oversight so that they can no longer be reliably directed, modified, or shut down by authorized people or systems,” the document reads.

The release comes amid an unprecedented focus on AI safety, driven by a string of rogue-agent incidents as well as the abrupt resignation of an Anthropic employee who cited the growing risk that AI would cause human extinction.

Together with Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI, Microsoft has broadly embraced a general approach of pacing the frontier, with particular support for embedded evaluators in AI labs.

“We welcome the research, focus, and deliberate pacing needed to get alignment right as the design goal,” Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella wrote online. “We also welcome ideas like “embedded evaluators” and the broader efforts to develop the mechanisms to make this more than just talk.”

data.title: Waymo opens robotaxi service in Las Vegas
data.description:
Waymo has begun to open up its robotaxi service to the public in Las Vegas, just a few weeks after receiving final approval from Nevada transportation regulators.

The Alphabet-owned company said Monday it will invite public riders on a rolling basis, following a robotaxi launch playbook it has followed in 14 other cities.

Waymo is starting with “dozens” of its new Ojai minivan robotaxis, which will serve an area of Las Vegas that includes the Strip south of Highway 589 and into Boulder Junction, according to a spokesperson. Waymo’s fleet and service area will eventually scale. For now, members of the public will have to request an invite and hope to receive an access code. Typically, Waymo opens the service up to everyone within a month or two of its official launch.

The announcement follows a busy few weeks for Waymo as it tries to ramp up its operations across the United States and Europe as Tesla, Zoox, and other competitors attempt to close on its lead. Earlier this month, the company began offering its robotaxis to invited members of the public in Denver, San Diego, and Tampa.

Las Vegas, where competitors Tesla, Zoox, and Motional are also planning to launch commercial robotaxi services, is Waymo’s 15th market. Waymo also operates in Austin, Dallas, Houston, Los Angeles, Miami, Nashville, Phoenix, and the San Francisco Bay Area. The company launched, and then paused service, in San Antonio.

Waymo’s entry into Las Vegas follows approval by the Nevada Transportation Authority to operate commercial robotaxi services in Clark County, home to Las Vegas. Tesla and Uber also received approval from the agency.

Waymo has been authorized to operate up to 1,000 autonomous vehicles over the next year, while Tesla is allowed to deploy up to 5,000, and Uber up to 1,000 robotaxis, which it will operate through partnerships with Hyundai subsidiary Motional and Zoox. Together, these permits would deploy up to 8,000 robotaxis across the county over the next 12 months.

It’s unlikely that the three companies will reach those numbers. Today, Waymo has a fleet of more than 4,000 robotaxis, which are spread across more than a dozen cities. Tesla’s Cybercab chief engineer Eric Early told state regulators, during a meeting in August, that he didn’t think the company would be “extremely happy and satisfied if we could get ourselves up to 2,500, maybe a bit higher than that in the next year.”

Even without reaching those figures, the city could be saturated with robotaxis in the next year.

data.title: Sources say Automattic’s board is out after failed attempt to oust CEO Matt Mullenweg
data.description:
Automattic’s board is out, multiple sources have confirmed to TechCrunch, after last week’s attempt to oust CEO Matt Mullenweg by voting to put him on a paid leave of absence.

After the vote, Mullenweg, the WordPress founder and CEO of WordPress.com parent company Automattic, accused the board of conspiring against him in a post on Automattic’s Slack. On Friday, TechCrunch exclusively reported Mullenweg told the company’s staff that he was back in control of the company, also via Slack post. Automattic confirmed to TechCrunch on Saturday that he had returned.

Initially, we heard from sources that Toni Schneider, a founding CEO at Automattic who now leads the open social network Bluesky, had resigned his Automattic board seat. Schneider has since removed a paragraph from his bio page on his personal website which had noted his contributions at Automattic.

Previously, Schneider’s website read: “I also contribute actively at Automattic, the open source company behind WordPress.com and WooCommerce. I was Automattic’s founding CEO and continue to support internal projects and investments as a board member and special advisor.”

We’ve also heard that Mullenweg removed the two other board members, Sue Decker and Gen. Ann Dunwoody.

Decker’s LinkedIn bio has been updated to confirm that she served on Automattic’s board from March 2020 through September 2026, despite her name still appearing on Automattic’s Board of Directors page at the time of publication.

When asked by TechCrunch about the board changes, Automattic declined to provide specifics, but offered a statement acknowledging that people have left.

Via an email that arrived after midnight PT on Sunday, an Automattic spokesperson shared the following:

“Matt and Automattic’s leadership team have great respect for everyone involved. While we can’t comment on specific individuals, we’re thankful for their contributions to Automattic and its mission, and we remain excited about what’s ahead with Matt at the helm. Matt was away for only 33 hours and 20 minutes—we’re now back to work,” the spokesperson said.

Given that these departed board members were those who voted to put Mullenweg on a paid leave of absence to begin with, it makes sense that a board shakeup has taken place. It also explains how Mullenweg’s return to his position as CEO would have the “full support of the board,” as a statement issued on Saturday indicated.

TechCrunch is hearing from sources Automattic may make an internal announcement about the new board sometime on Monday.

What prompted the board’s vote still remains unclear. Mullenweg and Automattic are involved in a high-profile lawsuit with a WordPress hosting company, WP Engine. Mullenweg has accused the company of infringing on the WordPress trademark and not sufficiently contributing in terms of engineering hours or money to the open source WordPress effort. Earlier this year, WP Engine claimed in a court filing that Automattic planned to target other competitors with royalty fees.

More recently, it has accused Mullenweg of allegedly destroying evidence related to the case in apps like WhatsApp, Signal, and Telegram. Last year, Mullenweg had deactivated the accounts of several WordPress contributors over alleged plans to fork the open source software.

Do you have more information? You can reach Sarah Perez at sarahp@techcrunch.com or @sarahperez.01 on Signal.

data.title: Superhuman acquires YC-backed notetaker Fathom as productivity platforms push for agentic work
data.description:
Superhuman is joining the cadre of productivity platforms launching notetakers — but rather than building one internally, it is acquiring Y Combinator-backed Fathom.

AI-powered productivity platforms aim to automate work. Typically, that automation is triggered when a user types prompts and creates workflows. It would be even better, however, if AI could proactively start work, and for that, the topics and action items discussed in meetings are key. Hence the desire by Superhuman and similar platforms to move into notetaking.

To date, Fathom, which was founded in 2020, has raised over $30 million in funding, and it was valued at $94 million in 2024, according to data from PitchBook. Its investors include Zoom Apps Fund, Telescope Partners, BoxOne Ventures, and Maven Ventures. Its cap table also includes individuals such as Reddit CEO Steve Huffman, former Twitch CEO Emmett Shear, and Cruise co-founder Kyle Vogt.

The notetaker offers a generous free plan, and that has resulted in over 400,000 monthly active users. The company said that over 1 million people have recorded meetings until now.

TechCrunch learnt that earlier this year, Superhuman tested a notetaker internally with select users, but eventually chose to acquire a finished product to integrate with its productivity suite, with AI at the center. Shishir Mehrotra, Superhuman’s CEO, acknowledged this; he said that in the process of testing, the company realized how hard it is to create a notetaker.

“We’ve been working internally on this area for a while as well. I think it greatly increased our confidence in the demand in this category. It also becomes very clear how deep the products in this category are and how much you need to build. A lot of these products make the job feel really easy, but it’s actually quite tricky to do a great job in all parts [of meeting recording],” Mehrotra told TechCrunch over a call.

Mehrotra said that he was impressed with some of the technical intricacies built by the Fathom team, but didn’t elaborate on which ones. He did tease that with a notetaker, Superhuman can work on surfacing meeting context in real time.

Competition in the meeting notetaker space is intense, and startups like Granola, Read AI, and new entrant Wispr have raised millions of dollars to aid that growth. Despite having a healthy customer base or revenue run rate, venture-backed notetakers are feeling the heat from the market to do more than just notetaking. Some of these factors did matter in Superhuman acquiring Fathom, while Fathom’s CEO Richard White said that Superhuman’s 40 million user base was a good opportunity to reach users at scale.

“The reach of Superhuman is massive. I have always thought about M&A in terms of speed of building a product that everyone uses, and a part of that comes down to distribution. If we were to operate Fathom as a standalone company, we would have to build a lot of things that are already in the Superhuman platform,” he said.

On the platform front, Superhuman already has an email client, a docs app, a calendar, a database solution, and a newly launched AI agent builder platform. With a meeting notetaker in the middle, Superhuman can draft emails, update data entries, schedule follow-up meetings, and have AI agents start work and extract insights from meeting data.

data.title: Hear how AI can engineer nature’s comeback at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
data.description:
Not long ago, bringing an extinct species back to life belonged to science fiction. Today, it’s the mission of a billion-dollar startup. Advances in artificial intelligence, genetics, and computational biology are changing what’s possible in conservation research, raising questions that extend far beyond the laboratory. If technology can help revive extinct species, should it? And what role should AI play in shaping the future of biodiversity? 

Those are the questions at the center of “Can We Engineer Nature’s Comeback?“, a Real World AI Stage fireside chat at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026.

Joining the conversation is Ben Lamm, Co-Founder and CEO of Colossal Biosciences, a company pioneering efforts to bring extinct species back through advances in synthetic biology and AI. Rather than focusing solely on the science, the discussion explores the technologies behind de-extinction, the role AI now plays in modern biology, and the growing debate over whether engineering nature represents a conservation breakthrough — or a distraction from protecting the ecosystems we already have.

Disrupt returns to Moscone West in San Francisco, October 13–15, bringing together 10,000+ founders, investors, and operators for 250+ sessions exploring the technologies and market forces shaping what’s next. Hear one of this year’s most provocative conversations. Secure your pass to Disrupt.

Where AI meets biology

AI is already reshaping software, robotics, and scientific research. Biology may be its next frontier. Researchers are using AI to analyze genetic data, model biological systems, and accelerate discovery. Companies like Colossal are pushing those advances even further, applying AI alongside synthetic biology to questions that until recently belonged in science fiction.

This session explores where those technologies intersect and what happens when AI moves beyond digital systems and into the natural world. For founders working at the intersection of deep tech, life sciences, and AI, it’s an opportunity to hear how one of the industry’s most ambitious companies is approaching problems few organizations have attempted to solve.

Explore the Real World AI Stage lineup and register for Disrupt today.

A founder building at the edge of what’s possible

Ben Lamm has spent more than two decades building companies at the intersection of AI and emerging technologies. A serial entrepreneur, he’s built businesses focused on solving complex challenges — from enterprise AI and critical infrastructure to conversational intelligence. Before founding Colossal Biosciences, he launched several pioneering technology companies, including Hypergiant, Conversable, and Chaotic Moon, which were later acquired by Trive Capital, LivePerson, and Accenture.

Today, he’s applying that entrepreneurial mindset to an entirely different challenge: using AI and synthetic biology to explore de-extinction as a conservation tool. That work has made Colossal one of the most closely watched — and most debated — companies in science and technology. As CEO, Lamm sits at the center of conversations about biodiversity, climate resilience, emerging technologies, and the responsibilities that come with engineering living systems.

His experience offers founders a rare look at what happens when breakthrough technology doesn’t just disrupt an industry, challenging how we think about what’s possible.

Join the conversation with one of tech’s most unconventional founders. Secure your Disrupt pass today.

A conversation bigger than de-extinction, only at Disrupt 2026

Reviving extinct species captures headlines. The broader questions may prove even more significant. As AI becomes part of scientific discovery, conversations about technology increasingly extend beyond software into medicine, biology, conservation, and climate science. Those advances bring new possibilities, but they also raise difficult questions about how, and where, these tools should be used.

Whether you view de-extinction as a scientific breakthrough, a conservation strategy, or a controversial experiment, the discussion reaches far beyond any single species. It asks what role emerging technologies should play in solving some of the world’s most complex problems and who gets to decide.

Lock in your pass to Disrupt with up to $200 in savings, and join the conversation about where AI, biology, and innovation intersect.
